title: British MPs use a secret ballot in a contested Speaker election
body: The Commons can confirm a former Speaker seeking to return by agreeing a motion. When no former Speaker seeks re-election or that motion fails, MPs choose a Speaker by secret ballot.
takeaway: Choosing who will chair a chamber can follow a different voting procedure from deciding its legislation.
source: UK Parliament, MPs' Guide to Procedure, Election of the Speaker

title: Singapore's Parliament includes appointed members
body: A parliamentary committee in Singapore can nominate up to nine people for appointment by the president as Nominated Members of Parliament. Their term is two and a half years.
takeaway: Appointment adds a route into the chamber distinct from winning an electoral district.
source: Parliament of Singapore, Special Select Committee and Educational Resources

title: A permanent UN member can abstain without using its veto
body: On a substantive UN Security Council vote, an abstention by a permanent member is not treated as a veto. A resolution can still pass if at least nine members vote in favour and no permanent member votes against.
takeaway: The published voting record can show that a country let a measure pass without supporting it.
source: United Nations Security Council, Voting System
